title: Strongly convex noisy value optimization with Schatten-Lipschitz Hessians and no curvature upper bound
summary: The full Schatten range p from two to infinity parameterizes Hessian regularity under independent Gaussian scalar values. The risk comparison separates large-budget asymptotics from all-budget lower bounds.

description_paragraphs: Minimize a hidden strongly convex objective globally on $\mathbb R^d$ using noisy scalar values, with terminal objective error as the loss.
task.formulation: Minimize a hidden strongly convex objective globally on $\mathbb R^d$ using noisy scalar values, with terminal objective error as the loss.

description_paragraphs:
For $p\in[2,\infty]$, $f:\mathbb R^d	o\mathbb R$ is $C^2$ and satisfies $$
abla^2 f(x)\succeq\mu I,\qquad\|
abla^2f(x)-
abla^2f(y)\|_{S_p}\leho\|x-y\|_2$$ for every $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$. The unique global minimizer obeys $\|x_*\|_2\le R$.

The Schatten norm $\|A\|_{S_p}$ is the ell-p norm of the singular values, with $S_2$ the Frobenius norm and $S_\infty$ the operator norm. There is no global upper bound on the Hessian or gradient. The known minimizer ball does not constrain queries or output.

description_paragraphs: One query at any $x_t\in\mathbb R^d$ returns $Y_t=f(x_t)+\xi_t$, where the noises are fresh independent $N(0,1)$ variables, independent of the algorithmic seed and past observations. Opposite-point observations have independent noise; no same-sample reuse or noiseless values are available.
Public inputs are $d,p,\mu,\rho,R$ and a horizon $T$ or target error $\varepsilon$. The objective is hidden.

Opposite-point observations have independent noise; no same-sample reuse or noiseless values are available. Public inputs are $d,p,\mu,\rho,R$ and a horizon $T$ or target error $\varepsilon$. The objective is hidden.

description_paragraphs: Return any measurable $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$ from the transcript, whether or not it was queried.
output.feasibility: Return any measurable $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$ from the transcript, whether or not it was queried.

description_paragraphs: The base loss is $f(\widehat x)-f(x_*)$. For a fixed horizon, the minimax risk is $$\mathcal E_T^{(p)}=\inf_A\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_{S_p}(d,\mu,\rho,R)}\mathbb E[f(\widehat x)-f(x_*)].$$ Expectation includes private randomization and observation noise.
metric.base_expression: The base loss is $f(\widehat x)-f(x_*)$. For a fixed horizon, the minimax risk is $$\mathcal E_T^{(p)}=\inf_A\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_{S_p}(d,\mu,\rho,R)}\mathbb E[f(\widehat x)-f(x_*)].$$ Expectation includes private randomization and observation noise.

description_paragraphs: Each scalar noisy value costs one evaluation. Repeated values, every side of a finite difference, localization, and validation are all charged. The algorithm uses at most $T$ evaluations on every execution. Exact specification of finite query coordinates, arithmetic, and storage are free.
resource.budget: Each scalar noisy value costs one evaluation. Repeated values, every side of a finite difference, localization, and validation are all charged. The algorithm uses at most $T$ evaluations on every execution. Exact specification of finite query coordinates, arithmetic, and storage are free.

components.description: Its accounting convention is stated in the resource paragraphs.

description_paragraphs: Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.
Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.
The expectation averages the independent Gaussian observations and private randomization after the function is fixed. The evaluation count is capped on every path.
